package.name: sidewalk_slam
package.description:
Phase 3-4 of the Mitacs sidewalk VSLAM project: make the robot able to build a map of a place it has never seen, and then find itself on that map again.
RTAB-Map is the PRIMARY mapping and localisation system, consuming ZED X depth, rectified colour and the camera's 200 Hz IMU. It produces both a 2D occupancy grid for navigation and a 3D point cloud map, in a single saveable, reloadable database, with separate mapping and localisation-on-an-existing-map modes.
Two comparative baselines run over IDENTICAL recorded input: the ZED SDK's own closed-source visual-inertial positional tracking, and ORB-SLAM3 in stereo or stereo-inertial mode. All three emit trajectories in one common TUM format so that the evaluation package can compare them directly. That three-way comparison on identical data is the core research contribution of the project.
The package also contains a build helper that adds the ROS layer of rtabmap_ros against the RTAB-Map core already installed on the Jetson (0.21.10, in /usr/local) rather than installing a second copy of it, a generator that writes ORB-SLAM3's settings file from live camera_info so the intrinsics can never go stale, and a validator that refuses to let a physically implausible run be treated as a result.
package.author: Thaw Zin
